support_amy: acme-inc reporting structured-json (json_mode) streaming responses truncated mid-object. Happened twice this morning ~2026-03-15 14:02 UTC. Client sees invalid JSON parse errors. Attaching truncated body and curl.
customer_ops: ```HTTP/1.1 200 OK\ncontent-type: text/event-stream\ndata: {\"id\":\"resp_123\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"user\":{\"id\":\"u-1\",\"email\":\"alice@acme.com\"},\"profile\":{\"name\":\"Alice\"}   \n\"meta\":{\"score\":0.92},\"last_message\":\"Thanks!\"}, \"finish_reason\":null}]\n\ndata: {\"id\":\"resp_123\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"extra\":\"more data here\"}\n```  <-- note final object cut off, missing closing braces
support_amy: curl they used: ```curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxxxx\" -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?json_mode=true\"``` they get parse error client-side when parser hits EOF.
eng_sre_jason: looking at edge traces for req-id req_987654321 shows upstream connection closed with 499 and message \"upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream\" at ~14:02:12. Any CDN/proxy hops? could be keepalive/idle timeout or proxy resetting long-lived connection.
customer_ops: customer is behind corporate gateway + CloudFront (we're origin). They said it happens when response is ~20-30s long and includes lots of small SSE frames.
eng_runtime_sahil: can you paste the full x-request-id/trace id? also did token refresh/rotation happen around then? we've seen auth refresh flow cause a 401 on subsequent fetch and some proxies close stream on auth error.
support_amy: request-id: req_987654321. From our app logs: \n\"stream: wrote chunk size=512\nstream: wrote chunk size=128\nstream: client closed connection: EOF (socket 10.1.2.3:52344 FIN)\"\nresponse body in logs ends at '...\"extra\":\"more data here\"' no trailing braces.
eng_sre_jason: edge snippet: \"[14:02:12] upstream read() returned 0, client prematurely closed connection, 499\" + CloudFront logs show Keep-Alive timeout of 15s. Customer proxy also logs TCP FIN at same second. This looks like midstream client FIN rather than server crash.
eng_runtime_sahil: mitigation ideas: 1) ensure we always emit a final sentinel event (e.g., data: {\"_complete\":true}\n\n or a final 'data: [DONE]') and flush before closing file descriptor. 2) add heartbeat every 8s to keep proxies from thinking stream is idle. 3) detect socket FIN and mark response as truncated for telemetry and surface to support.
billing_emma: heads up: customer also reported they were billed for tokens even though client never saw final object and retried. We should correlate billing events with request lifecycle so we can detect half-completed streamed requests and consider user-friendly billing adjustments or idempotency tokens.
eng_runtime_sahil: opening ENG-RUNTIME-1587 to track: \"streaming: final-flush + heartbeat + truncated-response telemetry\". I'll own patch and test with CloudFront in staging. For immediate repro: try curl with slow-read to simulate buffering: ```curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" \"https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?json_mode=true\" | pv -qL 10``` should reproduce drop if proxy times out.
deploy-bot: deploy at 2026-03-14T03:10:23Z: rolling update eng-runtime v2.7.1 (no streaming fixes in that release)
support_amy: ok setting P2, looping in @eng_runtime_sahil and @eng_sre_jason. Next steps: ask customer to bypass CF and retest, provide packet capture if possible, try the slow-read repro. I'll offer a temporary workaround: add keepalive comments every 6s and see if that stabilizes client parsing.
billing_emma: I'll flag potential invoice adjustment and await outcome.
support_amy: thanks — will follow up after customer test. :thumbsup:
